title: UK2000 Wick, Amazon Bush Strips & Global Fireworks! | MSFS 2020 Marketplace
description:
Are you looking to expand your global route network in Microsoft Flight Simulator this week, or are you trying to avoid impulse buys on the storefront? Today, we break down five brand-new scenery and visual releases on the MSFS 2020 Marketplace—spanning windswept Scottish coastal runways and remote Brazilian Amazon bush strips, before lighting up the night sky worldwide with global fireworks.

To help you decide what fits your flight logs and storage budget, we inspect these new Marketplace additions and detail what each developer brings to the platform:

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 EUROPEAN COASTAL GATEWAYS: WICK JOHN O'GROATS AIRPORT EGPC (UK2000 SCENERY)
We start at the northeastern tip of mainland Scotland, inspecting Wick John O'Groats Airport (EGPC) by UK2000 Scenery. Serving Caithness since 1933, this package upgrades the default airport with weathered roof textures, North Aviation buildings, custom ground vehicles including a VIP tractor, parked cars, and full seasonal textures. Please note that you will also need to install the free UK2000 Scenery Common Library.

🇧🇷 AMAZON BASIN REGIONAL AIRFIELDS: SBUA, SWHT & SWTP (HEAVEN DESIGNS & BLG)
Next, we head deep into the Brazilian Amazon for a trio of regional frontier airports by Heaven Designs and BLG:
• São Gabriel da Cachoeira (SBUA): Located in the upper Rio Negro region near the triple border of Brazil, Colombia, and Venezuela, featuring detailed cracked aprons, terminal buildings, and emergency services.
• Humaitá (SWHT): Set in the southern Amazon near Rondônia where rainforest meets open savanna, adding custom apron wear, upgraded foliage, and realistic regional airport details.
• Tapuruquara (SWTP): A remote rainforest airstrip near Santa Isabel do Rio Negro where riverboats and bush planes rule, complete with an updated terminal, aprons, and local scooters out front.

🎆 GLOBAL VISUAL EFFECTS: GLOBAL FIREWORKS (DREAMSCENERY)
Finally, we check out Global Fireworks by Dreamscenery, bringing celebratory pyrotechnics to 617 locations across 188 countries. Displays trigger on major real-world dates—including New Year's, 4th of July, Canada Day, Bastille Day, Lunar New Year, Diwali, and Bonfire Night—alongside scheduled shows at major theme parks in Anaheim, Orlando, Paris, Tokyo, Hong Kong, and Shanghai.

Whether you are braving North Sea crosswinds into Wick, river-hopping across the Brazilian Amazon, or flying evening approaches over glowing city skylines, we evaluate this ramp inspection to help you decide what truly deserves a spot in your simulator installation.

If you enjoy honest, clear, and critical looks at the Flight Simulator Marketplace without the fluff, make sure to hit that like button, subscribe to the channel for weekly sim coverage, and drop a comment below! Which of these new add-ons are you picking up first?
